readme:
# Baron Power Play

**Pay-per-call AI infrastructure for autonomous agents. USDC on Base, settled by Coinbase. No API key, no account, no subscription.**

Base URL: `https://baron-power-play.baronpowerplay.workers.dev`

---

## Why this exists

Agents fail at paid APIs in four predictable ways. Baron Power Play is built to remove each one.

| Agent failure | What Baron does about it |
| --- | --- |
| You cannot learn the price or the shape of a service before committing money | Every route publishes an exact x402 v2 challenge and a machine-readable contract. You know the cost to six decimal places before you send a single request. |
| A provider 429s halfway through your task and your agent dies | Several independent engines with automatic failover and a pooled daily capacity. A dead engine is invisible to the caller. |
| A third-party service can steer your agent with text smuggled into a response | Prompt-override attempts are blocked before payment, and model output is scanned before it is returned. |

If you are an agent, **read `/.well-known/x402.json` and `/openapi.json` first.** They are the contract. This README is the human-readable summary.

---

## Verify before you pay

This is free and it is the fastest way to decide whether to depend on us.

```bash
curl https://baron-power-play.baronpowerplay.workers.dev/test
```

It returns engine-by-engine health, a live inference result, and live checks of the market-data and voice paths. Run it whenever you are about to depend on this service, not once at signup.

---

## Services

| Endpoint | Method | Price (USDC) | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/infer` | POST | 0.001 | LLM inference. JSON and code are auto-formatted on the way out. |
| `/markets` | GET | 0.002 | DeFi TVL leaders, DEX trending pairs, meme category, watchlists, delta sync. |
| `/alpha` | GET | 0.05 | Trading notes with Kelly-Criterion position sizing. **No verified track record is published — treat this as research input, not a signal to trade.** |
| `/tts` | POST | 0.01 | Text to speech with emotion casting and a pronunciation dictionary that remembers per wallet. |
| `/stt` | POST | 0.01 | Speech to text with crypto-keyword detection and timestamped segments. |
| `/test` | GET | **free** | Readiness, engine health, and live capability check. |

`/alpha` accepts `portfolio_size_usd` as a query parameter.

---

## Payment

- **Network:** Base (`eip155:8453`)
- **Asset:** USDC, paid with an EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization`
- **Asset identity:** `USD Coin` version `2`
- **Protocol:** x402 v2 — HTTP 402 Payment Required
- **Facilitator:** Coinbase CDP (`https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402`)
- **Receiving wallet:** `0xb838930bf3dFD467D30979E12c0a94286F86708D`

The flow is the standard one. You send the request, you get a 402 with the exact payment requirement, you sign an authorization, you resend with the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header, and the facilitator settles on Base. **Work is only performed after Coinbase verifies and settles the payment.** No unpaid work, ever.

Amounts on the wire are in token atomic units. A 0.001 USDC call quotes as `1000` in `accepts[].amount`. The `amount` fields in `openapi.json` are decimal USD; the runtime `accepts[].amount` is atomic units.

---

## Capacity

Inference is pooled across several independent engines, selected by remaining headroom, with automatic failover, so a failing upstream is invisible to the caller.

Capacity resets at 00:00 UTC. When the pool is exhausted the route returns a machine-readable `SOLD_OUT` with a `Retry-After` and a comeback offer rather than a generic error.


`/markets`, `/alpha`, `/tts`, and `/stt` do not draw on the LLM engine pool.

---

## Limits and abuse controls

Per wallet, per day:

- 50 calls per endpoint (`/alpha`: 20)
- a lower cap during the wallet's first 24 hours
- $10 total spend
- 10 payment requests per second

Per request:

- `User-Agent` required, minimum 3 characters
- `POST` must send `Content-Type: application/json`
- bodies over 1 MB are refused
- query strings over 2000 characters are refused
- `X-Idempotency-Key` is optional, max 128 characters, restricted character set
- wrong HTTP method returns `405` with a machine-readable `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`

Reuse defenses:

- a used payment header is refused for 1 hour
- a used USDC authorization nonce is refused for 24 hours
- 5 rejected override attempts in an hour blocks that wallet for a day

Every error uses one shape, so you can branch on `code` instead of parsing prose:

```json
{
  "error": "/infer accepts POST, not GET",
  "code": "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED",
  "suggestion": "Use POST /infer.",
  "timestamp": 1790458945409
}
```

---

## Referrals

Refer a wallet and both sides benefit: the referred wallet gets 10% off its first paid call, and the referrer is credited 5% of the list price after settlement. Three referred calls per day maximum, no self-referral.

---

## Discovery

- `GET /openapi.json` — canonical OpenAPI 3.1 contract: request and response schemas, `x-payment-info` per route, error codes
- `GET /.well-known/x402.json` — x402 manifest: endpoints, prices, methods, facilitator, payment requirements, defenses
- `GET /test` — free health and capacity check

---

## Working with it

```bash
BASE=https://baron-power-play.baronpowerplay.workers.dev

# free readiness check
curl -s "$BASE/test"

# the machine-readable contract
curl -s "$BASE/openapi.json"

# see the exact payment requirement before paying anything
curl -si -X POST "$BASE/infer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: your-agent/1.0' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
# -> HTTP 402 with the x402 v2 challenge in accepts[]

# market data
curl -s "$BASE/markets"
```

To make a paid call, take the `accepts[]` entry from the 402, sign the matching EIP-3009 authorization with your wallet, and resend the original request with the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. Any x402 v2 client library does this for you.
